children: A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after recovering oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and a projected fourth-quarter global crude surplus pushed Brent crude below $93 per barrel.

Brent futures fell below $93 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate slipped to roughly $87, CNBC data revealed. The International Energy Agency reversed its earlier deficit call, projecting fourth-quarter supply will average 105 million barrels per day, 1.7 million bpd above demand, while detailing 71 million barrels in emergency reserve releases, including 15 million barrels of diesel, by late February.

Wall Street is already marking down longer-term crude assumptions: Goldman Sachs projected in a client note cited by CNBC that Brent will average $88 in 2027 and ease to $78 by year-end as oversupply builds. Still, BMI analysts cautioned in research carried by CNBC that OPEC+ export recovery remains fragile after unverified Iranian reports of tanker mine explosions in the Strait of Hormuz.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:

Zooming in on Atlas Energy Solutions

Atlas Energy Solutions’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 45 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 5 days ago when the stock gained 5% on the news that shipping attacks in the Persian Gulf sparked renewed supply concerns, driving crude oil prices sharply higher.

The Wall Street Journal reported that front-month Brent crude rose 1.2% to $92.55 a barrel, recovering from a sharp selloff. West Texas Intermediate futures rose 0.7% to $86.67. The Journal said the strikes tempered expectations of a diplomatic resolution to the U.S.-Iran conflict, and that supply risks in the region persist. A bottleneck in that shipping lane can tighten the crude available to buyers and add a geopolitical premium to the price. Higher oil prices can support revenue and cash flow for producers.

Atlas Energy Solutions is down 47.2% since the beginning of the year, and at $5.14 per share, it is trading 74% below its 52-week high of $19.75 from May 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Atlas Energy Solutions’s shares at the IPO in March 2023 would now be looking at an investment worth $302.95.
